_readme: Tracking file for site/scripts/download-covers.mjs. Each entry is one article's cover image candidate, found via web search on commons.wikimedia.org (Claude could not reach Commons directly from its sandbox — see chat). Run `npm install` once (adds the sharp dependency), then `node scripts/download-covers.mjs` from inside site/ on a machine with normal internet access. The script re-verifies license/author live against the Wikimedia API before downloading anything (never trusts the fields below blindly), requests a pre-scaled rendition rather than the raw original, compresses it into a hero (<slug>.webp) and a separate thumbnail (<slug>-thumb.webp) under public/images/covers/, and writes cover_image / cover_image_thumb / cover_image_alt / cover_image_credit into the matching content/<slug>.md front matter. On success the entry is deleted from this file. Entries only remain when something failed (status: 'failed', with a 'notes' explanation) or hasn't been attempted yet ('pending'); re-run any time to retry them.

images.suggested_alt: Weathered marble bust of Socrates with a broad nose and full beard, photographed against a plain dark background
images.notes: Roman 1st-century marble, Louvre; search snippet reports CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Series article 1 of 6. Chosen for tonal consistency with the Plato and Aristotle busts queued below.

images.suggested_alt: Marble portrait bust of Plato, bearded and looking slightly downward, photographed against a plain background
images.notes: Vatican Museums (Pio-Clementino), Roman copy after a 4th-century BCE Greek original. Series article 2 of 6.

images.suggested_alt: Marble bust of Aristotle with short curled hair and a trimmed beard, photographed against a plain background
images.notes: Palazzo Altemps; Roman marble copy of a lost bronze by Lysippos, c. 330 BCE. Note the alabaster cloak is a modern addition, so avoid describing it as ancient in the alt text. Series article 3 of 6.

images.commons_file_title: File:Frans Hals, Portrait of René Descartes (cleaned up).jpg
images.suggested_alt: Painted head-and-shoulders portrait of Rene Descartes in dark clothing with a white collar, turned slightly toward the viewer
images.notes: Frans Hals, c. 1649. PD (author died 1666; published before 1931). Filename carries the accent in 'René' exactly as on Commons. If the API lookup fails, the same painting is also at 'File:Frans Hals - Portret van René Descartes.jpg'. Series article 4 of 6.

images.suggested_alt: Painted portrait of Immanuel Kant in eighteenth-century dress, seated and facing slightly to one side
images.notes: Anonymous painter, c. 1790 -- so the script's author extraction will probably fall back to 'an unlisted Wikimedia Commons contributor'; a hand-edited credit naming the anonymous c.1790 portrait may read better. Series article 5 of 6.

images.suggested_alt: Black-and-white studio photograph of Friedrich Nietzsche in 1882, seated in a dark suit with a heavy moustache, looking away from the camera
images.notes: Gustav Adolf Schultze, Naumburg, early September 1882 -- one of five from that sitting. Same year as The Gay Science, which the article discusses. PD (photographer died over 100 years ago). Series article 6 of 6.
